title: Retract a quick-change arbor's pin collar, thread a 2-1/2 in hole saw on to align the drive pins, and lock it
instruction: Pull the arbor's pin collar down, screw the hole saw onto the arbor, short of bottoming out, until its two pin holes line up over the drive pins (back it off if it reaches the stop), then push the collar up so both drive pins lock through the hole saw.
context: Mounting a hole saw on a quick-change 2-pin arbor requires pulling the detented collar down so its pins clear the shoulder, screwing the 2-1/2 in cup onto the 5/8"-18 thread short of bottoming out until its two 7.8 mm backplate holes line up over the retracted 6.35 mm drive pins (backing off if it hits the stop: tightening to the stop alone, an ordinary hold-and-turn, leaves the holes out of phase so the collar stalls on steel, and drilling without pins wedges the threads shut), then pushing the collar up through both holes. Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00, 821,000 US workers) and general maintenance workers (O*NET 49-9071.00, 1,621,800) swap bi-metal hole saws this way daily. Milwaukee's 49-56-7250 sheet states: "Screw the Hole Saw onto the arbor's thread; ensure hole saw is not bottomed out on threads. Align the pins with holes on the back of the hole saw and push the collar upward to secure the hole saw in place."
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, z up from the bench. At (22.5, -1.5), an IRWIN 226340 forged-iron drill-press vise (textured 4 in / 10.16 cm jaws, 4-1/2 in / 11.43 cm jaw capacity, slotted base 17.8 x 13.4 cm, steel jaws 3.8 cm over the bench, screw handle towards +x; EU equivalent: BESSEY S10-ST or 100 mm drill-press vise) is bolted flat to the bench and clamps the 7/16 in (11.1 mm) hex shank of a Milwaukee 49-56-7055 Large Thread Quick Change Arbor (10.16 cm long, 222 g, hardened steel, 5/8"-18 UNF thread, nut-free sliding collar as on Milwaukee's 49-56-7250 sheet; EU 2-pin collar part: Milwaukee 4932479467 or Lenox 1779772 2L Snap-Back) upright within 1 degree of vertical, with its thread shoulder 10.5 cm over the bench and its two 6.35 mm drive pins (25.4 mm bolt circle) along +/-y (within 2 degrees) so the top camera sees both inside a mounted cup. The knurled 4.2 x 2.7 cm sliding collar (8.0 mm vertical stroke, ball-detent) starts in its upper detent (flush with the 10.5 cm shoulder, pins projecting 7.0 mm above the shoulder, red witness paint on the pin tips and white axial stripes at +/-y). At (22.5, +16.5), a 12 x 12 x 0.3 cm grey rubber mat is taped to the bench with white +/-y ticks. Centered on the mat (within 2 mm, backplate down, guarded rim up) is a Milwaukee 49-56-0147 2-1/2 in (63.5 mm) HOLE DOZER Bi-Metal Hole Saw (EU 49560147, 4.76 cm tall including a smooth black PVC U-channel edge strip over its upper teeth to protect the shared robot's finger pads; 195 g, 5.0 mm steel backplate with 5/8"-18 center bore and two chamfered 7.8 mm pin holes on a 25.4 mm circle), with its holes and red outer / white inner ticks along +/-y (within 3 degrees). In the simulation the tight shoulder stop lies 55 degrees clockwise past +/-y pin alignment (estimate); on real hardware the bought pair's thread starts fix that back-off angle (recorded in the first minutes and used if 20 to 140 degrees, else another 49-56-0147 cup is used); nothing varies by seed.
scoring: 0 for good if at any point in the trial the hole saw drops off the bench (underside more than 10 mm below bench level; on the bench, judged from the trial video). Otherwise read at the end of the trial. 1.0: the hole saw sits coaxially on the arbor (within 4 mm and 6 degrees of vertical) with a shoulder gap of at most 0.60 mm (a 0.60 mm feeler gauge cannot enter between the backplate and the arbor shoulder), its two 7.8 mm backplate holes are aligned within 8 degrees of the +/-y drive pins, the sliding collar is pushed within 1.5 mm of its upper stop (6.5 mm or more of its 8.0 mm upward travel, driving both 6.35 mm pins through the 5.0 mm backplate so both red pin tips show in the holes from above and the cup resists a gentle hand twist without turning), every part of both hands is at least 30 mm clear of the hole saw and collar, and both parts stay still (under 10 mm/s and 0.1 rad/s) for 1.0 s. 0.5: the hole saw is seated within the 0.60 mm shoulder gap with its two pin holes aligned within 8 degrees of the drive pins, without the collar locked within 1.5 mm of its upper stop (or before the 1.0 s clear hold ends). 0.25: the collar was pulled down at least 6.0 mm (within 2.0 mm of its lower stop, judged from the trial video) or the hole saw is threaded coaxially within 2.0 mm of the shoulder without aligned pin engagement (including a cup screwed tight to the +415 degree stop where the collar stalls on the solid backplate, or stopped half a turn early at 0.92 mm gap). 0.0: otherwise. On the bench: shoulder gap and collar travel with 0.60 mm and 1.5 mm feeler gauges or a caliper, pin engagement in both holes from the top photo and a gentle hand twist check, whole-trial drop, collar retraction, hand clearance and 1.0 s hold from the video.
reset_notes: Between trials, about 45 seconds: pull the arbor's sliding collar down 8 mm to retract the drive pins, unscrew the hole saw counterclockwise off the 5/8"-18 arbor, push the collar back up 8 mm into its upper detent (within 0.5 mm of flush with the shoulder, red pin tips 7 mm proud), place the hole saw backplate-down at the center of the grey mat at (22.5, +16.5) cm (within 2 mm) with its red barrel stripes and white inner ticks aligned to the mat's +/-y ticks (within 3 degrees), and verify that the black PVC tooth-rim guard sits snug all round and the vise holds the arbor upright (within 1 degree) with its two drive pins along +/-y (within 2 degrees).
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX; vise and arbor shaft fixed. The 5/8"-18 thread is a stand-in helical carrier (four 50 g gravity-balanced links, 1.411 mm/turn, 0.06 N m drag) catching coaxially on the retracted arbor, stopping at +415 deg (55 deg past pins, estimate), and releasing below 0 deg. The collar slides 8.0 mm on a 10 N bi-stable detent (assumed); two rigid 6.35 mm pins stall on the 5.0 mm plate unless within 8 deg of the 7.8 mm holes. Flutes and bare teeth omitted.
